Guidance & outlook: As indicated, the revenue is around INR402 crores, a 21% quarter -on-quarter increase compared to Q4 of FY26.
As you know, we came off from FY25 -- a very successful FY25 and FY26 results were not as expected because a lot of the deals we were expecting to close at the time didn't materialize.
So that's why the split between current split of India international is like 93% India and 7% international, and we hope to change that profile going forward.
Growth & demand: So I'll start with our revenues of Q1, which was INR402 crores, 20% growth over Q4.
Profit after tax improved slightly and same for order book, which also saw a small growth.
That's why at the end of the quarter, the order book was 93% domestic and 7% international.
Margins & costs: And then finally, optimizing our operating expenses in line with our business and cost engineering for improving margins and working capital management to reduce finance costs over time.
I would say our first target will be positive EBITDA and EBIT and then going to PAT profitability as well.

So I think your first question was about warranty costs, and they are usually determined by potential fault rates and repair requirements and anticipated claims during the warranty period, and is driven by our cumulative installed base.
Capex & expansion: On the debt side, the net debt increase is mainly, as what I mentioned earlier, due to net working capital increase as well as increased payouts, and also the company's focus in terms of continued investments in terms of capex.
And lastly, we are still awaiting the expansion order for the BSNL 4G with additional 26,000 sites.
So yes, there will be increase in our current product sales, but we also need higher capacity because networks will become higher capacity, and we are investing in that to evolve our products.
Balance sheet & cash: And at net receivable level, the net receivables after the customer advance adjustments currently stand at INR2,232 crores compared to INR1,905 crores.
The gross borrowing stands at INR4,866 crores and net borrowings at INR4,277 crores.
Just on the receivable, I see that the receivable has moved from INR1,900 crores to INR2,232 crores.
Risks & challenges: So their focus is on the software side for the 5G network, on the vRAN and so on.

So in a nutshell, whenever we make these products, I think those differentiators are built-in and designed and then the quality of your portfolio is what really matters in terms of being able to win over the competition that you're talking about.

Guidance & outlook: We ended with INR1,514 crores at the end of Q4 as opposed to INR1,019 crores at the end of Q4 of FY25.
We also received PLI incentives for FY25, an additional INR69 crores, reaching a total of INR469 crores for FY25.
Based on our FY27 business outlook, we believe that with our current investments and cost structure, we will be able to achieve better financial results.
Growth & demand: And as I mentioned, we had a significant order book year-on-year growth.
The revenue for the quarter 4 was INR333 crores compared to INR307 crores in the previous quarter, a quarter -on-quarter growth of 8%.
The full year revenue was INR1,103 crores and profit after tax of negative INR909 crores.
Margins & costs: The cost of memory does impact the cost of our products, even though it's a small component of our product cost.
And also, as a part of the increase, we are also renegotiating our costs, our prices with customers as well as for the new opportunities which are out there to make sure that we protect our margins.

Because, I mean, the purpose to ask this question was to understand how much should we expect the margin compression at the contribution margin level, because it's not only the memory, even the chip prices have sort of inched up because that demand for chips has also been higher.
Capex & expansion: The other significant thing was that we received an initial order for the expansion of 4G networks from a customer in South Asia.
Our high-capacity optical, which supports 1.2 terabit per channel, is going to scale to 1.6 terabit and beyond to support the terabit -scale data center connectivity of the future.

Our multi -terabit Tejas Networks Limited April 15, 2026 edge node is going to again scale in capacity and interface and also going to integrate with compute capacity and compute infrastructure to support edge AI applications.
Balance sheet & cash: Receivables at INR3,258 crores and payables at INR478 crores.
The cash position at the end of the quarter was INR505 crores and a net debt of INR3,531 crores.
At gross level, the borrowings were INR4,035 crores at the end of the quarter.
Risks & challenges: We had a lot of technical problems uploading other materials to the SEBI site and that largely caused the delay.
